briefs.headline: Exxon hits a record high after saying fuel-making profits jumped $4.5B
briefs.summary: On Friday, October 16, Exxon gave an early look at its July–September results. It said higher refining margins (the extra money it makes turning crude oil into fuels like diesel) added about $4.5 billion to its earnings. Wars in the Persian Gulf and Russia damaged fuel-making plants and pushed fuel prices up, which helped refiners like Exxon. The stock rose 2.5% that day and closed at a record $178.98, though lower oil prices and accounting timing effects will take a big bite out of the gain.
bull: Higher refining margins added about $4.5 billion to Exxon's third-quarter earnings, more than double what its fuel business earned in the second quarter.
Wars that damaged other companies' fuel plants pushed diesel prices to record highs, which helps Exxon's refineries.

Exxon expects a $2.5 billion accounting hit from 'timing effects' to reverse in later quarters. These are gains and losses on trading deals that get counted before the related oil shipments are finished.
bear: Lower crude oil prices are expected to cut $1.3 billion from Exxon's oil-drilling business, and weaker chemical profits will cost about $600 million.
Timing effects will lower reported earnings by about $2.5 billion this quarter. Earlier this year, the same issue helped push first-quarter profit down to $4.2 billion, its lowest in five years.
One analysis said that at a record $179, the stock price assumes fuel profits will stay unusually high for years. That depends on fuel shortages lasting.
